notes: Positives must fire intent-layer and run the script before proposing a node — state, then measure, table first, check as the gate. Negatives sit on the real borders: /prime (reads nodes, never writes), the rules layer (a path-scoped domain rule is setup step 5, not a node), skill-improve (this plugin's own artefacts), and a single /evolve learning capture that lands in an existing node without restructuring. One invocation per case id with --threshold 1.0; prose assertions use (?i) regex because responses capitalise sentence-initially. The script is invoked with a quoted path — python -X utf8 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.../intent_layer.py" state . — so every subcommand assertion allows the closing quote and the elided form (... check .); a regex written as intent_layer\.py\s+state failed four correct responses in round 1. The content assertions are English-keyword regexes: a session that answers in another language (a host CLAUDE.md that pins pt-BR, say) fails them on vocabulary, not on behaviour, so a clean-session run pins the language with --append-system-prompt "Answer in English." and says so in learning.md; the routing evidence (which skill was loaded) is read from the tool stream, not from the prose.

evals.prompt: Set up AGENTS.md for this repo so agents stop guessing where things live. It is a bun monorepo: apps/web, packages/api, packages/core, packages/types.
evals.expected_output: Fires intent-layer. Runs state first and shows it, then measure, and pastes the table before proposing anything. Names AGENTS.md as the root node and CLAUDE.md as behaviour beside it, not a second root. Proposes child nodes only where the table or a responsibility boundary justifies them, downlinks them from the root's Where things live table, and names check as the gate.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Runs the state subcommand before deciding.
Measures before proposing a node.
AGENTS.md is the root node; CLAUDE.md is not a second root.
Downlinks the children from the root.
Names the check gate.

evals.prompt: Agents keep editing packages/api when the logic they want is in packages/core, and our root AGENTS.md is 900 lines. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: Fires intent-layer. Diagnoses a root past its cap and a subtree with no node. Proposes splitting by ownership into child AGENTS.md files under packages/core and packages/api with a purpose line that says what each does NOT own, keeps the root as the downlink index, and cites the 4k-token cap and the 32 KiB Codex chain.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Names the node cap or the Codex chain limit.
Splits by ownership into child nodes.
The purpose line says what the subtree does not own.
Measures rather than guessing which subtrees earn a node.

evals.prompt: Which directories in this repo deserve their own AGENTS.md? I do not want one in every folder.
evals.expected_output: Fires intent-layer. Runs measure and pastes the table, applies the signals — 20k tokens, 64k split, responsibility boundary, hidden contracts at the nearest ancestor, cross-cutting at the lowest common ancestor — and says explicitly which directories get nothing and why. Excludes tests and small utility folders.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Runs measure and shows the table.
Applies the token threshold, by number or by the verdict vocabulary.
Says which directories get nothing.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(not every directory|no node|gets? nothing|do(es)? not (earn|need) (a|one|its own))

assertions.description: Names a responsibility boundary or the lowest common ancestor as a signal.
Runs state before measure — the procedure's first step, which an unaided answer skips.

evals.prompt: Execute AGENT_SETUP.md step 4b for this project. The root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md were just rewritten in 4a.
evals.expected_output: Fires intent-layer as the step's implementation. Runs state, then measure with the table shown, decides with reasons, captures from the repository before asking, writes nodes and downlinks, runs check and quotes its exit code, and produces the one-line Intent layer entry for the Step 11 report.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Runs state first.
Runs check and reports its exit.
Sources node content from the repository before asking a person.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(from the repository|git log|manifest|before asking|one question at a time)

assertions.description: Produces the report line for Step 11.

evals.prompt: Audit our AGENTS.md files. Some of them describe modules we deleted last quarter and I think a couple are never linked from anywhere.
evals.expected_output: Fires intent-layer in maintenance mode. Runs check for orphans, dangling downlinks, oversized nodes and placeholders; re-asks the capture questions for the stale ones; reports drift between a node and the tree rather than silently rewriting it; offers audit and candidates as the two maintenance moves.

assertions.description: The skill fires by name.
Runs the check gate.
Looks for orphans and dangling downlinks.
Reports drift rather than silently rewriting.

evals.prompt: Load the context I need to work on the checkout flow before I start.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /prime, which reads the root AGENTS.md, the matching rules and the nearest node under the frontend or backend root. Writes nothing, runs no measure, proposes no new node.

assertions.description: Routes to the context loader.
Does not run measure or propose a new node.
Reads rather than writes.

evals.prompt: Write a rule that every database call goes through the repository layer, and make it load automatically whenever someone touches src/db/**.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the rules layer: a file under .claude/rules with a paths: frontmatter matching src/db/**, per setup step 5 and templates/rules. Not an AGENTS.md node — a rule loads on path match, a node is read on entry.

assertions.description: Routes to the rules layer with a paths: field.
Does not create an AGENTS.md node for it.
Does not run the intent-layer script.

evals.prompt: My skill in this plugin does not fire — I think its description overlaps another skill's. Audit the wiring.
evals.expected_output: Routes to skill-improve (Mode B, trigger collision and wiring audit). No AGENTS.md hierarchy work, no measure, no node.

assertions.description: Routes to skill-improve.
Does not run the intent-layer script.
Does not propose an AGENTS.md node.

evals.prompt: We just fixed the date-boundary bug in the reports aggregation. Capture the learning so it does not recur.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /evolve: appends the dated learning to the log and to the existing nearest AGENTS.md section. Does not restructure the hierarchy, does not run measure, does not create a new node — the intent-layer skill is loaded by /evolve only when the subtree has no node or the node is over its cap.

assertions.description: Routes to the learning capture flow.
Appends to an existing node or log rather than restructuring.
Does not run measure.

evals.prompt: Review whether our AGENTS.md is still accurate for this change; suggest fixes only. AGENTS.md:8 says routes live in src/routes/. The approved diff against release-base removes src/routes/api.ts, adds src/http/api.ts, and updates src/server.ts:3 to import ./http/api. An untracked src/http/health.ts also exists. Identify only contradicted instructions and the smallest correction, with evidence/confidence. Do not rebuild our hierarchy.
evals.expected_output: Reports the contradicted route-location rule at AGENTS.md:8, supported by removal of src/routes/api.ts, new src/http/api.ts and src/server.ts:3 importing it; states impact, minimum src/http/ correction and confidence. Respects release-base and relevant untracked scope without inferring health.ts ownership. Advisory only; no hierarchy construction.

assertions.description: Attributes the stale rule to its actual AGENTS.md:8 origin, not merely the audit method.
Identifies the removed route location and the concrete replacement plus its current consumer.
Explains why the stale route instruction matters.
Recommends only updating the route instruction to the evidenced src/http boundary.
States a confidence score from 1 to 5 inline or in the declared table score cell; a header scale alone is insufficient.
Reports actual no edits applied, not the future effect of the suggested correction.

evals.prompt: Check our instructions against this patch, without editing. AGENTS.md:12 says run npm test; package.json:8 changed scripts.test to scripts.check, and CI now runs bun run check. A staged change updates the runner; the unstaged part is its call site. Report the instruction affected, contradictory current evidence, impact, minimal fix and confidence.
evals.expected_output: Identifies AGENTS.md:12/npm test as stale, ties script rename test to check and CI/current runner evidence to bun run check across staged and unstaged changes, gives validation impact, minimum instruction correction and confidence without edits.

assertions.description: Preserves the instruction source AGENTS.md:12 and the contradicted npm test command.
Uses the changed script and CI evidence, not a package-manager preference alone.
Recommends the current bun run check command as the minimum correction.
Explains the effect on validation.
States a confidence score from 1 to 5 inline or in the declared table score cell; a header scale alone is insufficient.
Reports actual no edits applied, not the future effect of the suggested correction.

evals.prompt: Our root AGENTS.md says all DB calls use src/repositories. A child AGENTS.md does not repeat it. The diff only adds src/services/report.ts calling src/repositories/report.ts. Audit whether the inherited instruction needs an update; no edits authorized.
evals.expected_output: Returns no finding/update: the root AGENTS.md rule remains inherited and the new service uses src/repositories/report.ts. The child need not repeat the rule; preserve the existing hierarchy and make no edits.

assertions.description: Identifies the root AGENTS.md as the inherited source rather than treating the child as missing a rule.
Returns no rule correction for valid inheritance.
Grounds compliance in the actual repository-layer call.
Rejects duplicating the ancestor rule in the child.

evals.prompt: Review only a punctuation correction in README.md. Paths, build commands, consumers and invariants are unchanged. Do we need to audit or rebuild the full AGENTS.md hierarchy? Explain the smallest appropriate action, without edits.
evals.expected_output: Explains that punctuation-only README scope has no changed instruction-bearing path, command, consumer or invariant; no semantic audit or hierarchy rebuild is justified and no edits are made.

assertions.description: Bases the scope decision on punctuation-only change.
Declines the irrelevant audit or hierarchy reconstruction.
Names the unchanged semantic boundaries that make the diff irrelevant.
Stops at an advisory no-drift result without recommending a rewrite; actual tool traces separately verify zero successful writes.

evals.prompt: The diff renamed src/jobs to src/workers; AGENTS.md:6 still names src/jobs. I asked for review only. Give the rule/source, evidence, impact, minimal recommendation and confidence, and state the mutation outcome.
evals.expected_output: Reports AGENTS.md:6/src/jobs contradicted by rename to src/workers, the misdirected-work impact, minimum recommendation and confidence. Explicitly reports no mutation; advisory findings never edit consumer instructions, even if a surrounding review offers --fix.

assertions.description: Attributes the target rule to AGENTS.md:6 in a rule/source statement or origin cell, not merely elsewhere in the response.
Grounds the contradiction in the exact old/new directory rename.
States the practical impact of the stale destination.
Recommends the minimum workers reference correction.
Explicitly records no edits/mutation, rather than claiming the recommendation was applied.
States a confidence score from 1 to 5 inline or in the declared table score cell; a header scale alone is insufficient.
Does not assign target-rule authority to node-anatomy or assert an unsupported target downlink structure; separate method citations and explicit cautions remain valid.
